Class ComponentBuilder

java.lang.Object
io.github.isoyigido.basic.gui.core.loader.ComponentBuilder
Direct Known Subclasses:
ImageComponent.ImageComponentBuilder, TextComponent.TextComponentBuilder
public abstract class ComponentBuilder extends Object

Represents a Builder for Component objects. Subclasses of this class must add required and optional parameters in a parameterless constructor and override the build() method to provide the component building logic using the added required and optional parameters. A component declaration in a GUI file which is missing any required parameter will be ignored.

Required parameters may be added using addRequiredParameter(String, Parameter), and optional parameters may be added using addOptionalParameter(String, Parameter). Adding parameters using these methods effectively ties the given key in the GUI file to the given parameter. For example, if addRequiredParameter("color", colorParameter) is used, and GUILoader encounters the field color in the component declaration, the corresponding value will be parsed and set for colorParameter using setParameterValue(String, String).

To allow usage in GUILoader, subclasses of this class must be annotated with RegisterComponentBuilder. Subclasses of this class annotated with RegisterComponentBuilder are registered statically in ComponentBuilderRegistry.

Example usage:
In the example below, components of type button in the GUI file will use a new instance of ButtonBuilder for creation. The button declaration must include width, height, and color parameters; while it could also include a label parameter.

@RegisterComponentBuilder(type = "button")
public class ButtonBuilder extends ComponentBuilder {
    // - Initialize parameter fields -
    private final IntegerParameter width = new IntegerParameter();
    private final IntegerParameter height = new IntegerParameter();
    private final ColorParameter color = new ColorParameter();
    private final StringParameter label = new StringParameter();

    public ButtonBuilder() {
        // - Add required and optional parameters in the constructor -
        super.addRequiredParameter("width", this.width);
        super.addRequiredParameter("height", this.height);
        super.addRequiredParameter("color", this.color);
        super.addOptionalParameter("label", this.label);
    }

    @Override
    protected Optional<Component> build() {
        // - Get required parameter values -
        int width = this.width.get();
        int height = this.height.get();
        Color color = this.color.get();

        // Component building logic with optional parameters...
        Button button = new Button(width, height, color);
        this.label.getOptional().ifPresent(button::setLabel);

        // Return an optional of the component
        return Optional.of(button);
    }
}

API Note:
Multiple ComponentBuilder implementations may exist for a single Component type. For example, a component builder of type img-path and a component builder of type img-resource could both build the same type of image component, while one could load the image from the given path and the other from the given path relative to the resources folder. Furthermore, a single ComponentBuilder implementation may allow for multiple ways to declare the component by making use of optional parameters. For example, a component builder of type image may have optional path and resource parameters, and load the image based on whichever one the user uses in the component declaration. In the case where the user uses neither, or an illegal combination of both, the build() implementation would return an empty Optional and preferably log a warning. When the build() method returns an empty Optional, the component declaration is ignored.

    • addRequiredParameter

      protected void addRequiredParameter(String key, Parameter<?> parameter)
      Adds a required parameter. The parameter key can consist of lowercase letters, uppercase letters, digits, underscores (_), and hyphens (-).
      Parameters:
      key - the key for the parameter
      parameter - the parameter that is effectively tied to the key
      See Also:
      • Parameter
      API Note:
      Required parameters must have a set value. The buildNewObject() method ensures that every required parameter has a set value before building the object, and returns an empty Optional if any required parameter does not have a set value. Implementations of build() can safely use Parameter.get() on a required parameter without checking if the parameter has a set value.

    • addOptionalParameter

      protected void addOptionalParameter(String key, Parameter<?> parameter)
      Adds an optional parameter. The parameter key can consist of lowercase letters, uppercase letters, digits, underscores (_), and hyphens (-).
      Parameters:
      key - the key for the parameter
      parameter - the parameter that is effectively tied to the key
      See Also:
      • Parameter
      API Note:
      Optional parameters may not have a set value. Implementations of build() must use Parameter.getOptional() on optional parameters to get an Optional of the value, or check whether the optional parameter has a value using Parameter.isPresent() before using Parameter.get(). Using Parameter.get() on a parameter that does not have a set value causes an UnsupportedOperationException to be thrown.

    • buildNewObject

      public Optional<Component> buildNewObject()

      Builds an object using the stored parameter values.

      Special cases:

      • Logs a warning and returns an empty Optional if any required parameter does not have a set value
      • Returns an empty Optional if build() returns an empty Optional
      Returns:
      an Optional containing the built object, or an empty Optional if any required parameter does not have a set value, or if the provided set of parameter values cannot be used to construct an object

    • build

      protected abstract Optional<Component> build()

      Override this method to provide the building logic using the stored parameters.

      This method is called in buildNewObject() after verifying that each required parameter has a set value.

      If the implementation of this method returns an empty Optional, the buildNewObject() method returns an empty Optional as well.
